_note: Complete short poems, all public domain. Slot 147.
Add poems by editing this file - the slot needs no code change. Keep them
SHORT and COMPLETE: the point of the slot is a poem finished in one
morning, with no serial to keep up with.
TRANSCRIPTION: these texts are transcribed and have NOT been diffed against
a canonical source. They print verbatim and are attributed by name, so an
error here is an error attributed to a real poet - the exact failure
SYSTEM.md section 9 exists to prevent. Each entry carries a `source` for a
verification pass. Treat that pass as outstanding.
PUBLIC DOMAIN: every author died before 1930 or the work was published
before 1929. Deliberately no translations - a modern translation of Basho
is under its translator's copyright even though Basho is not, and an old
public-domain translation has to be sourced rather than recalled.

poems.title: I'm Nobody! Who are you?
poems.author: Emily Dickinson
lines: Then there's a pair of us!
Don't tell! they'd advertise – you know!
To tell one's name – the livelong June –

poems.title: In a Station of the Metro
poems.author: Ezra Pound
lines: The apparition of these faces in the crowd;
Petals on a wet, black bough.

poems.title: A man said to the universe
poems.author: Stephen Crane
lines: A man said to the universe:
"The fact has not created in me

poems.title: Upon Julia's Clothes
poems.author: Robert Herrick
lines: Whenas in silks my Julia goes,
Next, when I cast mine eyes and see
That brave vibration each way free;
O how that glittering taketh me!

poems.title: November Night
poems.author: Adelaide Crapsey
lines: The leaves, frost-crisp'd, break from the trees

poems.title: Loveliest of trees
poems.author: A. E. Housman
lines: Loveliest of trees, the cherry now
Is hung with bloom along the bough,
And stands about the woodland ride
Now, of my threescore years and ten,
And take from seventy springs a score,
It only leaves me fifty more.
And since to look at things in bloom
About the woodlands I will go
To see the cherry hung with snow.

poems.title: "Hope" is the thing with feathers
poems.author: Emily Dickinson
lines: And sings the tune without the words –
And sweetest – in the Gale – is heard –
And sore must be the storm –
That could abash the little Bird

poems.title: Pied Beauty
poems.author: Gerard Manley Hopkins
lines: Glory be to God for dappled things –
For skies of couple-colour as a brinded cow;
For rose-moles all in stipple upon trout that swim;
Landscape plotted and pieced – fold, fallow, and plough;
And áll trádes, their gear and tackle and trim.
All things counter, original, spare, strange;
Whatever is fickle, freckled (who knows how?)
With swift, slow; sweet, sour; adazzle, dim;
He fathers-forth whose beauty is past change:
